what: The model bank: compile once, fit thousands of times
title: brms studies: the model bank and model_grid()
text: naive brms simulation study recompiles Stan model every task — minutes C++ compilation per seconds sampling. BrmsFitter() avoids model bank: start run_simulation(), distinct model spec fit_grid compiled (via brms::brm(chains = 0)), every task reuses compiled binary stats::update(recompile = FALSE). Two properties control : precompile (default TRUE): build bank run start. Set FALSE fall back fresh brms::brm() per task (sensible tiny studies debugging). bank shipped mirai daemons per run, parallel workers reuse binaries. brms warn recompile = FALSE used structurally incompatible data — silently reuse binary wrong model frame. bayesim therefore compares Stan data structure (via brms::make_standata()) compiled template task’s data, aborts run loudly mismatch. data_grid rows produce data different shapes (e.g. varying factor levels), either make structurally identical set precompile = FALSE. brms default priors data-dependent (example, intercept prior can centered using response template dataset). constants embedded compiled model refreshed update(recompile = FALSE). Therefore, always supply explicit priors every brms_model() precompile = TRUE; bayesim raises fatal configuration error model-bank row omits (opt BrmsFitter(allow_default_priors = TRUE) deliberately want template-derived priors). Use precompile = FALSE task-specific default priors part study design.

what: Case study: comparing likelihoods for skewed data
title: brms studies: the model bank and model_grid()
text: likelihood best describes right-skewed data — Gaussian, Student-t, lognormal? Generate skewed data, fit three models, compare expected log predictive density (ELPD): Three models compile exactly ; 150 fits reuse binaries.
code: skew_generator <- function(data_spec, task_ctx) {   n <- data_spec$n   x <- stats::rnorm(n)   mu <- data_spec$beta * x   y <- exp(mu + stats::rnorm(n, sd = 0.5))   list(     train = data.frame(y = y, x = x),     test = NULL,     response = "y",     true_params = c(beta = data_spec$beta),     vars_of_interest = "beta"   ) }  config <- simulation_config(   data_grid = data.frame(n = 200, beta = 1),   fit_grid = model_grid(     gaussian = brms_model(       y ~ x, brms::brmsfamily("gaussian"), explicit_priors     ),     student = brms_model(       y ~ x, brms::brmsfamily("student"), explicit_priors     ),     lognormal = brms_model(       y ~ x, brms::brmsfamily("lognormal"), explicit_priors     )   ),   data_generator = skew_generator,   fitter = BrmsFitter(chains = 2L, iter = 1000L, warmup = 500L),   metrics = list(     elpd_loo_metric(),     posterior_summary_metric(),     sampler_diagnostics_metric()   ),   n_replicates = 50L,   seed = 42L )  result <- run_simulation(config, workers = 4) summarize_simulation(result, metrics = "elpd_loo__elpd")

text: bayesim ships three fitters: LinearRegressionFitter() (exact conjugate inference, Stan), BrmsFitter() (Stan via brms, compile-model bank), CmdStanFitter() (.stan programs via cmdstanr). use different backend, implement custom fitter extending Fitter class. core contract deliberately small: implement fit_model() extract_draws(), opt optional capabilities declaring matching supports_* property method.

title: Custom Fitters
text: public fitter contract : matrices draws x observations (S x N) — predicted_samples, log_lik_matrix(), predict_epred() put posterior draws rows observations columns, matching brms/loo convention. single common custom-fitter bug; validate_fitter(smoke_test = TRUE) rejects transposed matrices. generics avoid masking common names: loo_fit (loo::loo), log_lik_matrix (brms::log_lik), fit_model (generics::fit).

title: Custom Fitters
text: fitter fits linear model OLS synthesizes posterior draws bootstrapping residual variance. executable without Stan.
code: library(bayesim)  # Define the class LinearFitter <- S7::new_class(   "LinearFitter",   parent = Fitter,   properties = list(     name = S7::new_property(S7::class_character, default = "linear"),     supports_predictions = S7::new_property(S7::class_logical, default = TRUE),     supports_log_lik = S7::new_property(S7::class_logical, default = TRUE),     supports_loo = S7::new_property(S7::class_logical, default = FALSE),     n_draws = S7::new_property(S7::class_integer, default = 500L)   ) )  # fit_model(): estimate the model and package draws S7::method(fit_model, LinearFitter) <- function(fitter, data_bundle, fit_spec, seed, task_ctx) {   train <- data_bundle$train   fit <- lm(y ~ x, data = train)   coefs <- coef(fit)   vc <- vcov(fit)   draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(fitter@n_draws, mu = coefs, Sigma = vc)   colnames(draws) <- c("intercept", "slope")    # Package into the supported public fit-result type. The engine validates   # and canonicalizes the draws at the task seam.   bayesim::new_fit_result(     fit = fit,     draws = draws,     diagnostics = list(       rhat_max = 1.0, ess_bulk_min = as.numeric(fitter@n_draws),       ess_tail_min = as.numeric(fitter@n_draws), divergent = 0L     ),     timing = list(total = 0, warmup = 0, sample = 0),     success = TRUE,     warnings = character(0),     error = NULL,     data_bundle = data_bundle   ) }  # extract_draws(): return the draws matrix S7::method(extract_draws, LinearFitter) <- function(fitter, fit_result, variables = NULL) {   fit_result$draws }  # predict_fit(): posterior-mean predictions # Convention: predicted_samples is S x N (draws as rows, observations as cols), # matching log_lik() and predict_epred(). S7::method(predict_fit, LinearFitter) <- function(fitter, fit_result, newdata = NULL, seed = NULL) {   data <- if (is.null(newdata)) fit_result$data_bundle$train else newdata   # draws is S x P; design matrix X is N x P, so draws %*% t(X) is S x N.   X <- as.matrix(cbind(1, data$x))   preds <- fit_result$draws %*% t(X)   list(     predicted_mean = colMeans(preds),     predicted_samples = preds,     predicted_sd = apply(preds, 2, sd)   ) }  # log_lik_matrix(): per-observation log-likelihood of each draw S7::method(log_lik_matrix, LinearFitter) <- function(fitter, fit_result, newdata = NULL) {   data <- if (is.null(newdata)) fit_result$data_bundle$train else newdata   fit <- fit_result$fit   sigma2 <- sum(residuals(fit)^2) / fit$df.residual   X <- as.matrix(cbind(1, data$x))   mu <- fit_result$draws %*% t(X)   residual <- sweep(mu, 2, data$y, "-")   # matrix: draws (rows) x observations (cols)   -0.5 * log(2 * pi * sigma2) - residual^2 / (2 * sigma2) }  # fit_diagnostics() S7::method(fit_diagnostics, LinearFitter) <- function(fitter, fit_result) {   fit_result$diagnostics }

The estimands (Intercept, slope x, sigma) are # recorded as true_params; bayesim surfaces them as truth__* columns. linear_dgp <- function(data_spec, task_ctx) {   n <- data_spec$n   beta <- data_spec$beta   x <- stats::rnorm(n)   y <- 1 + beta * x + stats::rnorm(n)   list(     train = data.frame(y = y, x = x),     test = NULL,     response = "y",     true_params = c(Intercept = 1, x = beta, sigma = 1),     vars_of_interest = c("Intercept", "x", "sigma")   ) }

text: performance measures Morris et al. (2019) characterise estimator across replicate datasets: bias — estimator hit truth average? empirical SE (emp_se) — variable estimator across datasets? MSE — mean squared error, combined bias-plus-variance. coverage — nominal interval contain truth nominal rate? model SE (model_se) — average uncertainty method reports (compare empirical SE check method’s uncertainty calibration). Monte Carlo estimate n replicates, carries MCSE — simulation’s standard error. Reporting performance estimate without MCSE like reporting sample mean without standard error: reader tell signal noise. bayesim computes every MCSE . title: Required number of replicates for a target MCSE — n_replicates_for_target
text: Inverts Monte-Carlo standard error (MCSE) formulas used performance_measures() return number replicates n required achieve target MCSE. Useful planning simulation study (precision / power calculation) running . MCSE formulas (Morris et al. 2019; rsimsum) invert : coverage (binary 0/1 outcome): MCSE = sqrt(p (1 - p) / n)  =>  n = p (1 - p) / MCSE^2. default p = 0.5 conservative max-variance case (maximises p (1 - p) therefore gives largest required n). continuous metrics (bias / mean / model SE): MCSE = sd / sqrt(n)  =>  n = (sd / MCSE)^2. Requires assumed standard deviation assumed_sd per-replicate point estimate (e.g. guess empirical SE estimator). returned value ceiling(n) always whole number replicates.

title: Simulation-method performance measures with Monte-Carlo standard errors — performance_measures
text: condition cells fixed data-generating truth, computes Morris, White & Crowther (2019, Stat Med) estimator-performance measures: bias, empirical SE, MSE, coverage, average model SE, n_sim, MCSE. truth varies across replicates (prior-predictive SBC study), fixed-truth Morris names returned. Instead, error distribution described mean_error, error_sd, error_mse; coverage average model SE remain available. parameter function pairs data-generating truth__<param> column per-task posterior_summary__*__<param> columns (point estimate mean, posterior sd, interval q_lower/q_upper). Coverage uses interval available; otherwise falls back coverage__by_param__<param> column present. Fixed-truth MCSE formulas follow Morris et al. / rsimsum: bias MCSE = sd(est - truth) / sqrt(n) empSE MCSE = sd / sqrt(2(n-1)) MSE MCSE = sqrt(Var((est-truth)^2) / n) coverage MCSE = sqrt(p(1-p) / n) modelSE MCSE = sd(posterior_sd) / sqrt(n) bias MCSE uses sd estimation errors est - truth, valid fixed varying truth alike (fixed truth truth constant, sd(est - truth) = sd(est)). varying truth, mean_error uses sd(est-truth) / sqrt(n), error_sd uses error_sd / sqrt(2(n-1)), error_mse uses sqrt(Var((est-truth)^2) / n).
